claims.claim: Quanta is structurally exposed to the physical bottleneck between grid/load growth and usable power infrastructure: utilities and load centers require transmission, distribution, generation and specialty construction capacity, while Q2 2026 evidence shows demand converting into record backlog and revenue growth.
Customer concentration is not presently a structural fragility: no customer represented 10% or more of consolidated revenue or receivables at June 30, 2026.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: specialty construction/self-perform capacity is required to convert grid and load-center capex into energized infrastructure

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: demand spans utilities, generation and load centers rather than a single customer

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: technology choices can change, but physical interconnection, transmission and distribution work remains necessary; project deferral remains a substitute for near-term spend

risks.risk: Skilled-labor, permitting, customer capex timing and large-project execution can shift the bottleneck from demand to delivery capacity.

causalEdges.mechanism: new generation/load cannot serve users without interconnection, transmission and distribution buildout
causalEdges.falsifier: utility/load-center capex remains strong while Quanta backlog and revenue contract materially

causalEdges.mechanism: delivery capacity converts contracted infrastructure demand into revenue and earnings
causalEdges.falsifier: sustained revenue growth fails to produce earnings/cash conversion because execution costs absorb scale benefits

unknowns.unknown: Project-level cancellation protections and margin mix are not fully established here.

claims.claim: A customer-concentration bear case is not supported by the current filing because no customer exceeded 10% of consolidated revenue or receivables in the relevant periods.
The stronger challenge is execution quality: rapid workload growth can expose labor, project timing, retainage/working-capital and acquisition-mix risks even when end demand is strong.

factors.name: concentration risk
factors.basis: current 10-Q reports no >=10% revenue or receivable customer

factors.name: execution risk
factors.basis: large projects and rapid scaling can create margin and working-capital volatility

risks.risk: Backlog is not equivalent to risk-free future revenue; project timing, customer financing and execution can alter conversion.
Acquisitions and project mix can obscure organic comparability and margin durability.

causalEdges.mechanism: more simultaneous large projects increase labor, scheduling and working-capital demands
causalEdges.falsifier: Quanta sustains margin/cash conversion while backlog scales without material execution slippage

unknowns.unknown: No independent canonical valuation/crowding conclusion is asserted.
